body: I will investigate using our GitLabCI example https://gitlab.com/cypress-io/cypress-example-docker-gitlab

@avatsaev and @bahmutov no need to investigate related to CI. This does not appear related to CI or containers at all.

How do I know?

Because the summary shows `zero` failures - even though we clearly picked up the failure when the test failed.

This should be reproducible in any environment on any system. @avatsaev we would really need a minimal reproducible amount of test code that causes this. Can you remove every single line of test code until the bare minimum to reproduce this?

The juggle of test failures to exit codes is one of the most tested places in Cypress - and its unlikely this is simple to reproduce on our end from the information you've provided. I'm guessing there is something that makes your situation unique which causes this to happen.

I only have one test, and I've used mochawesome reporter from the docs here: https://docs.cypress.io/guides/guides/reporters.html#npm-Reporters

I'm not sure what else I can provide as info, but the setup was pretty simple, just followed the official docs, I had to go back to protractor because apparently, support for third party reporters is buggy in cypress. There is still open issues related to reporters #551
I didn't realize mochaawesome was the source of the problem. We'll get it fixed.

After doing some research the issue appears to be more complicated. `mochawesome` does not correctly hold the number of `failures` on its `stats` property - which is what we use to denote exit code unfortunately.

I'm going to have to dig into their source code to see where they handle exit code and why it's different. A quick test shows me that when failures occur in `beforeEach` hooks they do not consider that a failure - which is why this is happening to you.

issue.title: Aggregate failures from mocha runner instance and not a reporter's stats object

labels.name: pkg/server
labels.description: This is due to an issue in the packages/server directory

repository.name: cypress
repository.description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

issue.body:
Reporters have different implementations and are not a reliable way to aggregate failures for exit codes when running `cypress run`.

Here's an example of `mochawesome` doing it different than standard mocha reporters. https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/1063

In this case, mochawesome treats `hooks` differently than tests and test failures are missed. O_O

We could aggregate these failure ourselves but mocha runner instances have a `failures` property that we can use instead. This should represent the most reliable way to bubble up failures.
